factors.name: Splitting and connector mix
factors.summary: Token split (0.88) and Connector Heterogeneity (0.81) load highly, so the factor reflects nets with more outgoing arcs at transitions and a more even mix of parallel and choice connectors, which suggests parallel splitting. Connector Heterogeneity also loads 0.57 on Factor 2 and Density loads 0.48 here, so the factor is not cleanly separated. It rests on two measures in a non-identified solution with a possible Heywood case for Connector Heterogeneity.

factors.name: Density versus choice-split complexity
factors.summary: Density (0.78) and Control flow complexity (-0.82) load with opposite signs, so denser nets tend to have lower control flow complexity in this dataset. This likely reflects that small nets are dense while large nets with many split arcs are sparse, but the factor rests on only two measures. Connector Heterogeneity (0.57) also loads moderately here.

factors.name: Residual factor
factors.summary: No measure loads above 0.14 and the factor explains only about 1% of the variance (eigenvalue 0.20). It is an artefact of extracting more factors than the data support and should not be interpreted.

interpretation.overall: Bartlett's test is significant and the overall KMO of 0.72 is acceptable, but after the MSA filter only four measures remain. The eigenvalues (3.14, 0.59, 0.20, 0.08) point to a single factor, as suggested. Most of the shared variance is therefore one general dimension on which Token split, Connector Heterogeneity and Density load positively and Control flow complexity loads negatively. Extracting three factors exceeds the Ledermann bound, so the varimax split into Factors 1 and 2 is not unique, and Factor 3 is empty. A one-factor solution, or a re-run with more measures retained, would be more defensible.
caveats: Three factors for four measures exceed the Ledermann bound, so the solution is not identified and the loadings are not unique.
Connector Heterogeneity has a communality of 0.995, which suggests a possible Heywood case.
The eigenvalues support only one factor, so the separation of Factors 1 and 2 is likely arbitrary.
Eight measures, including Size, were removed by the MSA filter, which limits how broadly the result can be read.
Connector Heterogeneity is undefined for nets without connectors, which may affect the sample.
Factor 3 explains about 1% of the variance and has no assigned measures.
